decision: Prospective application-level physical quality for a separate Weld and Pulley fixture. The four older traces keep their parity role and measured residual failures.

weld-rigid.geometry: A fixed 10 m by 0.5 m rectangle at the origin and a dynamic 1 m by 0.5 m rectangle centered at (0,2) m. The joint world anchor is (-0.5,2) m. The Weld spring is enabled at 8 Hz with damping ratio 0.3; equal angular limits [0,0] rad are enabled. Gravity is (0,-9.8) m/s^2. The dynamic body starts with velocity (2,0) m/s and a queued force (0,-10) N applied at world point (0.5,2) m before step 1. No later body or joint mutation.
weld-rigid.meaning: A softly constrained welded 1 m member may move by at most 1 cm at its shared anchor and rotate by at most one degree relative to the fixed member at every post-step sample.

pulley-taut.geometry: Two dynamic radius-0.5 m circles start at (-1,0) and (1,0) m. Fixed pulley anchors are (-1,1) and (1,1) m. Body anchors start at their centers. The ratio is 1 and the rope starts at 2 m. Slack is disabled. Gravity is (0,-9.8) m/s^2. The second body starts with velocity (0,2) m/s. No later body or joint mutation.
pulley-taut.meaning: The taut 2 m rope may depart from its fixed total length by at most 1 cm at every post-step sample. Both extension and compression count.

metric_definition: Weld anchor gap is Euclidean distance between getAnchor1 and getAnchor2. Weld angular error is the shortest directed angle from the joint's initial relative angle to getAngularTranslation. Pulley error is |distance(getAnchor1,getPulleyAnchor1)+distance(getAnchor2,getPulleyAnchor2)-getLength| with ratio exactly 1.
basis: The limits express an application choice: one-centimetre attachment play on a one-metre member, one degree of relative orientation, and one-centimetre rope-length play on a two-metre rope. They are neither dyn4j solver stopping tolerances nor limits fitted to recorded maxima. A baseline failure remains a failure.
